output.title: When spot checks stop working
output.body:
If you run a small business, spot checks are useful until they stop being reliable. The warning sign is not that you are inspecting too little on purpose. It is that the same errors keep showing up, or new ones slip through between checks. At that point the question changes from “should I inspect more?” to “which part of this workflow can be checked automatically, and which part must stay human?”

A good first candidate is a repeatable document or data review with clear rules. Think invoice amounts against an expected limit, customer replies against a simple FAQ list, or recurring form fields that should match a known pattern. That is not about replacing judgment. It is about making the routine flagging consistent so you only review exceptions.

The boundary stays firm: money movement and other high-risk decisions still need human approval. Automation can sort, flag, and route. It should not approve on its own.

For Bareni, the practical next step is a free 30-minute diagnostic of one recurring workflow. The point of that conversation is plain: does AI fit this task at all, where does it stop, and what would a clean pilot scope look like if it does fit? If spot checks keep failing, the next clarity step is to name exactly which check fails most often.
